title: A pinned input binding whose producer node was deleted is reported as healthy — the resolver never checks the producer still exists
rationale: D96/D103. `resolveInputPort` short-circuits on the lock list and returns `{status:"locked", ctxKey}` from the persisted `inputs[]` row without ever looking up the producer that `__auto.<nodeId>.<port>` names. `computeNodeInputIssues` treats only ambiguous/unsatisfied/locked-unbound as problems (apps/frontend/src/features/workflow-builder/auto-wire-status.ts:57), so a pinned port bound to a deleted node rolls up as `ok`: no badge, no drawer row, no warning. `resolvePinnedSource` even has a documented branch for exactly this case and chooses to render the raw `__auto.…` key as the source label (apps/frontend/src/features/workflow-builder/settings/input-row-resolution.ts:63) rather than flag it. The workflow saves clean and the engine injects `undefined` for that port (apps/temporal/src/graph-engine/node-executors.ts:381). Silently destructive with no design-time signal at all.

title: A ctx key with consumers and zero producers is never flagged — the binding walk skips it and the auto-wire warning is deliberately suppressed for it
rationale: D32/D33/D34/D105. `walkCtxKeyBindings` bails with `if (producers.length === 0 || consumers.length === 0) continue;` — a ctx key that nothing writes is never type-checked and never reported. The undeclared-key check (validator.ts:681/:697) only asserts the key has a *declaration*, not a *producer*, and the declaration survives node deletion (nothing prunes `config.ctx`). On the frontend, `autoWireIssuesToValidationErrors` explicitly excludes ports bound to a real (non-auto) ctx key from the 'needs a source' warning (apps/frontend/src/features/workflow-builder/auto-wire-validation.ts:34), and `effectiveResolution` renders them as the display-only `ctx-bound` state reading 'from <key>' (settings/input-row-resolution.ts:122). Net: delete the sole producer of a hand-authored ctx key and every consumer still reads as satisfied on every surface. 'Producer-less ctx key' is a state the model can reach but the design never named.

title: Activity-output cache key omits `activityType`, so a swapped or re-created node can be served the previous activity's cached output as a cache hit
rationale: D12/D78/D79 crossed with D98. The cache row is keyed `(workflowLineageId, node.id, sha256(stableJson(node.parameters)), inputHash)` — `activityType` is not a key component (the dynamic-node path had to smuggle its versionId *into* `parameters` to get any type identity into the hash: apps/temporal/src/graph-engine/node-executors.ts:338). Two reachable collisions: (a) swap a node from activity A to activity B where the reconciled parameters are equal — extremely common because non-overlapping schemas both collapse to `{}` (apps/frontend/src/features/workflow-builder/canvas/swap-node-type.ts:154) — and B is skipped and served A's output; (b) delete a node and add a new one of the same type, which reuses the freed id because `makeNodeId` fills the lowest free slot (apps/frontend/src/features/workflow-builder/WorkflowEditorV2Page.tsx:1543). Both present as a violet 'cache hit / skipped' badge and a populated preview, i.e. wrong data shown as correct data.

title: `errorPolicy.fallbackEdgeId` dangles on edge or node delete, is a hard validator error, and no settings surface exists to repair it
rationale: D50/D55. No delete path sweeps `errorPolicy.fallbackEdgeId`: neither the edge filter in `removeNodesFromConfig` (apps/frontend/src/features/workflow-builder/canvas/WorkflowEditorCanvas.tsx:1680) nor `deleteSelected` (WorkflowEditorV2Page.tsx:735) nor the direct-edge-delete branch of `handleDelete` (WorkflowEditorCanvas.tsx:2400). The validator then emits a blocking `Fallback edge "…" does not exist` error, and the backend rejects the save. But `errorPolicy` has no editor anywhere under `settings/` — `EdgePicker` is never mounted for it — and edge ids are randomly minted (canvas/wire-mutations.ts:28), so the referenced id can never be recreated. Combined with the absence of undo (D-011) this is the one cascade that is genuinely unrecoverable inside the builder: the workflow can be opened but never saved again.

title: Activity-type swap carries `outputs[]` verbatim, so stale output bindings write `undefined` into the ctx keys downstream consumers read
rationale: D97/D98. `swapActivityType` returns `outputs: node.outputs` unchanged (canvas/swap-node-type.ts:163) while `activityType` changes. The engine then writes `result[binding.port]` for every persisted output row — for a port the new activity does not return that is `undefined`, silently overwriting the ctx key downstream consumers are bound to. The canvas keeps drawing the wire because `buildProducerIndex` indexes `producerNode.outputs` directly and only *decorates* with the catalog (apps/frontend/src/features/workflow-builder/canvas/derive-wires.ts:105), so the graph still looks correctly wired. The swap carry-over is specified (WORKFLOW_BUILDER_GUIDE.md 'keeps … ports'), but what happens when the new type does not declare those ports is not.

title: Nothing ever checks that a `PortBinding.port` is a port the node's catalog entry declares
rationale: D19/D96/D107. There is no port-name membership test anywhere in the validator; `resolvePortKind` does `descriptors.find(p => p.name === portName)` and silently falls through to the ctx-declared kind and then to `undefined` on a miss, which makes `isAssignable` pass vacuously — so an orphan binding also disables the type check on that ctx key. `computePortRows` enumerates the catalog, not the bindings (apps/frontend/src/features/workflow-builder/canvas/port-rows.ts:139), and `portsForFooter` in the advanced editor does the same for activity nodes, so no UI can see or delete an orphan binding. Yet `deriveDataWires` still emits a wire for it and the canvas falls back to node-level handles to keep xyflow from dropping it. Reachable by an activity-type swap (D98) or by a catalog port rename between releases.

title: Activity-type swap carries `metadata.lockedInputPorts` / `lockedOutputPorts` verbatim, pinning ports the new type does not declare
rationale: D99/D104. `swapActivityType` returns `metadata: node.metadata` unchanged (canvas/swap-node-type.ts:167), so the lock list survives the schema change. `stripRedundantLocks` deliberately keeps a lock whose port has no binding ('keep — unusual, but preserve explicit intent'), and `normaliseLocks` re-infers on load, so the stale entry is durable. The lock is invisible (no row renders for an undeclared port) but live: if the new type later gains a port with that name, the resolver will refuse to auto-wire it and report `locked-unbound` with no explanation the author can act on.

title: `HumanGateNode.fallbackEdgeId` is never validated, so a deleted fallback edge passes validation and fails only at run time
rationale: D51. The only `fallbackEdgeId` checks in the validator are scoped to `node.errorPolicy` (validator.ts:335-:366); the humanGate branch at :905 checks the timeout duration only. So a gate with `onTimeout: "fallback"` whose edge was deleted saves clean and detonates at execution. Its sibling `errorPolicy` case (D-004) at least errors. The EdgePicker in HumanGateNodeSettings does show its own stale-reference warning, but only if the author happens to open that node.

title: `SwitchCase.edgeId` / `SwitchNode.defaultEdge` dangle after an edge or node delete with no delete-time signal
rationale: D48/D49/D55. No delete path prunes switch case references. The validator does flag them as errors (validator.ts:544, :550, :561) and `EdgePicker` computes a `staleReference` warning, so this is recoverable — but only reactively: the author gets no signal at the moment of deletion, and the reverse case (an edge nothing references) degrades gracefully to an `(unmatched)` label on canvas while the forward case does not degrade at all. The asymmetry is the gap: the same event produces a visible label change in one direction and a hidden dangling id in the other.

title: Entry-node reassignment on delete picks an arbitrary survivor, unannounced, and usually produces an immediately invalid graph
rationale: D3. Both delete implementations do `Object.keys(nodes)[0] ?? ""` (also canvas/WorkflowEditorCanvas.tsx:1683). Insertion order carries no topological meaning, and the validator forbids an entry node with incoming edges (validator.ts:277), so the auto-picked node is frequently invalid the instant it is chosen. There is no notification — the only signal is a workflow-level row in the validation drawer, which does not light the node badge because the anchor `entryNodeId` does not start with `nodes.`. Deleting the last node yields `entryNodeId: ""` and a hard 'entryNodeId is required' error.

title: No undo and no confirmation on any destructive builder action
rationale: Cross-cutting over every §3 edge. The config is a plain `useState` with no history stack, no snapshot ring and no Ctrl+Z handler; the trash icon, the context menu's 'Delete node' and the Delete/Backspace key all mutate immediately. That is what turns each individual dangling-reference finding above from an annoyance into a data-loss event: a single keystroke can destroy a node, its edges, the entry pointer and an arbitrary number of cross-references, and the only escape is to not press Save. A minimal fix is a confirm on multi-element delete plus an undo-toast for single deletes; a full history stack is a larger piece of work.

title: Two divergent node-delete implementations; the settings-panel one bypasses `resolveBindings` so the resolver never re-runs after a panel delete
rationale: D102/D103. `deleteSelected` is a hand-copy of `removeNodesFromConfig` (canvas/WorkflowEditorCanvas.tsx:1674) and calls `setConfig` directly, whereas every canvas-originated mutation goes through `handleCanvasConfigChange`, which wraps the new config in `resolveBindings` (WorkflowEditorV2Page.tsx:357). So the partial self-heal — rebinding an orphaned consumer to an alternative upstream producer — happens after a canvas delete but not after a panel delete, until some unrelated canvas interaction happens to trigger it. Same event, two different graphs. It also means the two copies will drift the moment either gains a reference sweep.

title: Ctx-key rename does not rewrite `metadata.inputs/outputs[].path`, which is a hard validator error with no repair UI for an existing library
rationale: D42/D45. `renameCtxKeyInConfig` returns `{...config, ctx, nodes}` — `config.metadata` is never touched, so `LibraryPortDescriptor.path` keeps naming the old key. For a library workflow `walkLibraryPaths` then errors at validator.ts:1631 ('does not resolve to a declared ctx key or node output'). `SaveAsLibraryModal` only ever creates a fresh lineage, so there is no surface that edits an existing library's port paths — the workflow is stuck invalid. The drawer's own copy promises 'renaming a key rewrites every binding that references it', so this is an implementation shortfall against a stated contract, not an unspecified case.

title: Ctx-key rename does not rewrite source-node produced keys, silently splitting producer and consumer
rationale: D31/D45. Source nodes write ctx directly from `parameters` — `source.upload`'s `parameters.ctxKey` and `source.api`'s `parameters.fields[].name` — and the validator treats those as declared producers (`collectSourceProducedCtxKeys`). The rename's `default:` branch rewrites only `inputs`/`outputs`, so after a rename the source keeps producing the old key while consumers read the new one. The canvas data wire from the source disappears (derive-wires rebuilds the producer index from the parameters) but the consumer's port row still reports `bound: true`, so the row reads as satisfied while pointing at nothing.

title: Ctx-key rename collision is a silent no-op and leaves the Name field displaying the rejected new name
rationale: D45. The guard `if (oldKey === newKey || newKey === "" || config.ctx[newKey]) return;` rejects a collision by doing nothing. Because the parent config is unchanged, the row's `ctxKey` prop does not change either, so the effect that re-syncs `localName` never fires and the input keeps showing the name the model rejected. The author believes the rename happened. There is also no identifier validation on rename at all (contrast `NEW_CTX_KEY_RE` on the creation path in VariablePicker), so `"my key"` or a dotted name is accepted and silently breaks root-key resolution everywhere.

title: Deleting a ctx declaration consumed only by map / join / childWorkflow ctx fields produces no validation error at all
rationale: D36/D38/D39/D40/D41. `validatePortBindings` walks only `node.inputs` / `node.outputs`; `map.collectionCtxKey`, `map.indexCtxKey`, `join.resultsCtxKey` and `childWorkflow.inputMappings/outputMappings` are never checked for declaration. (Switch/pollUntil condition refs *are* covered by `validateExpressions`.) The drawer's delete control offers no usage count, no reverse lookup and no confirm — it is a one-line object rest-spread. So deleting a key that only a map or a child-workflow mapping reads saves clean and fails at run time. The same walk also early-returns entirely when `config.ctx` is absent (validator.ts:663), so a source-driven workflow with no declarations gets no binding validation whatsoever.

title: Ctx declarations are never garbage-collected — implicitly created keys and keys orphaned by node deletion accumulate silently
rationale: D105. `declareCtxKey` is called from five settings surfaces via the VariablePicker's '+ Create variable' affordance and writes `{type:"object"}`; nothing anywhere removes a `config.ctx` entry except the drawer's manual trash icon. Removing the binding that motivated the key, or deleting the node that produced it, leaves the declaration behind, and an inert `object` declaration is invisible to the validator. Harmless in isolation, but it accumulates in every saved version and any such key later marked `isInput` leaks into the public run-spec. Deferrable because the failure mode is clutter, not incorrect execution — but it should be recorded rather than rediscovered.

title: Retyping `CtxDeclaration.kind` never re-checks consumers already bound to that key
rationale: D46/D20. `CtxDeclaration.kind` is only step 2 of `resolvePortKind` — a fallback reached when the catalog port has no kind. So when both producer and consumer are catalog-typed the ctx kind is ignored entirely, and when neither is, both sides resolve to the *same* ctx kind and `isAssignable(K, K)` is trivially true. Only the mixed case errors. The VariablePicker will dim newly-incompatible rows, but only for future picks; existing bindings are never revisited. A retype that should invalidate half the graph is therefore silent in two of the three configurations.

title: Renaming or retyping an `isInput` ctx declaration silently rewrites the workflow's public run-spec input contract
rationale: D43. `deriveFromCtx` builds the run-spec JSON Schema directly from `config.ctx` entries flagged `isInput`, using the declaration's key as the property name and its `type` verbatim. So an in-editor rename or type change silently changes the request body every existing API caller must send, and the curl sample in the run drawer changes with it. Nothing warns that the key is part of an external contract; the drawer renders `isInput` as an ordinary checkbox column. `CtxDeclaration.type` is otherwise not validated against anything in the graph, so this is its only real consumer.

title: `map.collectionCtxKey` never re-resolves once set, so deleting its producer leaves it permanently dangling with no check
rationale: D36. The map pass in `resolveBindings` skips any map whose `collectionCtxKey` is already truthy, so the auto-fill that originally chose the producer can never correct itself after that producer is deleted. Nothing in the validator checks that `collectionCtxKey` has a producer (it is not walked by `validatePortBindings` either — see D-016), and the element-kind lookup `resolveMapElementKind` just returns `undefined`, which also silently removes the map's synthetic producer from auto-wire candidacy for every node in the body. The map card shows no problem; the body nodes just quietly become unsatisfiable.

title: Node ids are reused after deletion, letting a new node inherit the deleted node's cache rows, run status and preview
rationale: D11/D12/D106. `makeNodeId` scans upward from suffix 1 and returns the first id not currently in `config.nodes`, so deleting `document_split_1` and adding another `document.split` reissues the same id. Node id is a key component of the activity-output cache (`ActivityOutputCache.nodeId`), of `NodeStatusesMap` and of the preview batch query, and none of those are pruned on delete. This is the mechanism that makes D-003's cross-node cache hit reachable, and it also means a replayed run paints the new node with the dead node's status circle and preview. A monotonic counter, or stamping a random suffix, removes the whole class.

title: `ExposedParam.path` is only checked as far as the node id — a path naming a parameter key that no longer exists is never reported
rationale: D28/D8. The validator splits the path and tests only `parts[1]` against the node id set; `parts[3]` (the parameter key) is never compared with the node's `parameters` or the catalog schema. The editor's 'stale' warning is likewise computed purely from group membership, and the `path` field is bare free text with no picker. So a catalog parameter rename, or a swap that drops a parameter key (swap-node-type.ts drops keys absent from the new schema), leaves the exposed param pointing at nothing with no signal on any surface. Minor only because the blast radius is a group's exposed-parameter form rather than execution.

title: Removing a key from an activity's `parametersSchema` leaves the saved value on the node forever, invisible and uneditable
rationale: D25. The form renders from `Object.entries(schema.properties)`, so a saved key with no property is never shown, and the write-back spreads the existing object and only touches the edited field, so the orphan survives every edit. No activity `parametersSchema` uses `.strict()`, so Zod strips the key during validation and reports nothing. The value is inert at run time (the activity ignores it) — hence minor — but it inflates the cache `configHash` input and makes two logically identical nodes hash differently, and there is no config-migration mechanism to clean it up (`SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSIONS` has one member).

title: Changing a discriminated-union parameter's discriminator wipes every sibling parameter with no prompt
rationale: D25. `onChange({ [union.discriminator]: v })` deliberately drops the previous variant's fields. That is defensible as a data model, but it is a destructive edit delivered through an ordinary Select with no confirm, no summary of what is being discarded, and no undo (D-011). Mis-clicking the strategy dropdown on a heavily configured node is unrecoverable. In-scope for Parts 3-9 because the rich-widget forms sit on top of exactly these unions.

title: `KindSelect` reads the frozen registry snapshot, so a dynamically registered kind renders blank and is overwritten on the next edit
rationale: D67/D63. `buildKindSelectOptions` iterates `Object.keys(ARTIFACT_REGISTRY)` — the `Object.freeze`d v1 snapshot, whose own doc comment says it does not reflect runtime registrations and that callers needing the live view must use `getArtifactKindMeta`. A kind added via `registerArtifactKind` therefore has no option, so `kindRefToSelectValue` hands Mantine a value absent from `data` and the field renders empty; the next `onChange` writes whatever the author picks over a kind they could not see. This is the mutation-axis half of the frozen-vs-live split: the read degrades gracefully everywhere else, but here it silently destroys the stored value.

title: An unregistered `pollUntil.activityType` is completely invisible on the canvas
rationale: D17/D16. When an activity type disappears from the catalog an `activity` node degrades legibly — `getActivityVisualHints` supplies a `❓` icon, an 'Unregistered activity.' description and the raw type string. A `pollUntil` node renders through the control-flow rectangle path, which never consults the activity catalog, so the same failure produces a normal-looking card. The only signal is the validator's node badge. `dyn.*` nodes get a dedicated red 'Deleted' badge, so the treatment of the same event differs across all three node flavours.

title: Renaming or removing a `source.api` field row silently orphans every consumer bound to it
rationale: D31/D30. The editor rewrites the whole `fields[]` array with no cascade to consumer bindings and no dialogue listing what depends on the row. The field is simultaneously a ctx producer and a run-spec input property (`deriveOutputSchema` → `buildRunSpec`), so one edit changes both the internal wiring and the external contract. Consumers get an undeclared-ctx-key error only if `config.ctx` is non-empty (validator.ts:663 early-returns otherwise), the auto-wire warning is suppressed because the port *is* explicitly bound (auto-wire-validation.ts:34), and the canvas drops the wire while the port row still reports `bound: true`. A rename is strictly worse than a removal: it produces an orphan binding and an unconsumed producer with nothing linking the two.

title: Exposed parameters are pruned silently on two of the three node-delete paths — only the settings-panel member removal raises the toast
rationale: D8/D58/D62. `pruneNodeFromGroups` returns only a config — the dropped count is reconstructed *by the caller* (`existingParams.length - prunedGroup?.exposedParams?.length`), so only `GroupNodeSettings.removeNodeId` can raise the 'Exposed parameter dropped' notification. The other two callers, `deleteSelected` (WorkflowEditorV2Page.tsx:745) and `removeNodesFromConfig` (canvas/WorkflowEditorCanvas.tsx:1686), have no mechanism to surface it. The canvas keyboard path deletes many nodes at once, so one keypress can silently destroy a whole group and all its exposed params. Test-plan 6.4 asserts the toast, which makes this look covered — it is covered only on the least destructive path.

title: 'Delete group' discards every exposed parameter with no confirmation, while removing the last member — the smaller act — does confirm
rationale: D57/D62. `deleteGroup` is a two-line object delete: member nodes survive (correct and documented) but `exposedParams` live only on the group object and vanish with it — no count, no toast, no confirm. Yet `removeNodeId` pops a `window.confirm` when removing the last member because that path deletes the group implicitly. So the guarded path is the incidental one and the explicit 'Delete group' button, which can discard N configured parameters, is unguarded. The inconsistency is the finding as much as the loss.

title: Re-grouping a node silently deletes its old group and leaves stale `exposedParams` on the group it was removed from
rationale: D56/D7/D8. `createGroupFromSelection` enforces single membership by stripping the incoming ids from every other group and dropping any group thereby emptied — taking its exposed params with it, unannounced (the success path in `handleGroupSelected` shows no notification; only the rejection path toasts). Worse, the *surviving* shrunken group has its `nodeIds` rewritten but its `exposedParams` left untouched, so an entry can keep naming a node that now belongs to a different group. That reference is dangling-but-valid: the node still exists, so the save-time 'references non-existent node' check never fires and `ExposedParamsEditor`'s stale badge (which tests group membership) is the only thing that can catch it.

title: A selected group chip is deletable but deleting it is a silent no-op, and `activeGroupId` is never cleared when its group is deleted
rationale: D59/D60. Chips are projected with `draggable: false` but no `deletable: false`, and `deleteKeyCode` is armed, so selecting a chip in simplified view and pressing Delete calls `handleDelete` with the synthetic id `group-chip-<id>`, which `removeNodesFromConfig` finds in no node map, edge list or group membership — nothing happens and nothing explains why. Neither reasonable interpretation (delete the group, delete its members) is offered or refused. Separately, `deleteGroup` never clears `activeGroupId`, so the right rail falls through to a 'Group not found. It may have been deleted or renamed.' placeholder rather than closing.

title: Deleting a library workflow is never blocked or even checked, and parents holding a `childWorkflow` reference to it still validate green
rationale: D69/D71. `workflowRef.workflowId` lives inside `WorkflowVersion.config` JSON, so there is no FK — the P2003 catch in `deleteWorkflow` can never fire for it, and unlike the dynamic-node path (which does a `config::text LIKE` scan before soft-deleting) nothing counts referencing workflows. Cross-workflow library port resolution is explicitly declared out of scope by the validator, so the parent saves clean with zero problems; the only signal is an orange 'Library not found (id may be stale).' line inside the child-workflow settings box, visible only if the author opens that node. At run time `get-workflow-graph-config` throws a plain retryable `Error`, so the parent burns its retry budget before failing. Blocker because the destructive action is on a *different* workflow than the one that breaks, and nothing links them.

title: `childWorkflow` input/output mappings are never checked against the library's declared port signature, and a missing output is silently skipped at run time
rationale: D40/D41/D70/D71. The library's `metadata.inputs/outputs` are fetched and rendered read-only, but the mapping rows are free-text `TextInput`s with no cross-check, no drift badge and no re-check on open; the only effect in the component re-seeds the inline-JSON draft. Because the reference is unpinned by default it follows head, so editing the child's signature silently breaks every parent. The executor writes an output mapping only `if (value !== undefined)`, so a mapping naming a port the child no longer emits produces no error anywhere — the ctx key just never appears, and the downstream consumer hits the producer-less-key blind spot of D-002.

title: Deleting a workflow lineage cascade-deletes every version, including versions pinned by completed runs and by other workflows' `childWorkflow` nodes
rationale: D70/D73/D74. `WorkflowVersion.lineage` is `onDelete: Cascade`. Ground-truth jobs (`Restrict`) and benchmark definitions (default `Restrict`) do block the delete, and `Document.workflowVersion` is `SetNull` — but runs are Temporal-side with no FK at all, so `RunSummaryDto.workflowVersionId` in the run-history drawer can point at a version row that no longer exists, and a `childWorkflow` version pin is just a number inside JSON that nothing scans. The protection model is therefore inconsistent by reference type rather than by consequence: the audit trail a run depends on is the least protected thing in the schema.

title: Soft-deleting a dynamic node breaks version-pinned nodes at run time, directly contradicting the documented contract
rationale: D76/D77. `apps/shared/prisma/schema.prisma:909` states that 'pinned versions of soft-deleted lineages continue to resolve at runtime'. The resolver throws `DynamicNodeDeletedError` on `lineage.deletedAt !== null` *before* the pinned-version branch is reached, so a node carrying an explicit `dynamicNodeVersion` fails anyway. This is the one place in the repo where the delete cascade was actually designed — the delete endpoint counts referencing workflows, the tombstone supports restore-on-republish, and the canvas shows a red 'Deleted' badge — which makes the divergence between the stated contract and the implementation the more important thing to fix: authors were told pinning protects them.

title: Nothing ever evicts an activity-output cache row on node delete, node retype or workflow delete — and there is no FK to clean up behind a deleted lineage
rationale: D12/D78/D83. `deleteExpired()` is the only delete on the table and it filters on `expiresAt` alone; the hourly GC is the sole caller. `ActivityOutputCache.workflowLineageId` is a bare `String` with no `@relation`, so even deleting a whole workflow leaves its rows behind for the full 24 h TTL. Harmless on its own, but it is the reservoir that makes D-003 and D-021 exploitable: rows for nodes that no longer exist stay live and reachable by any future node that lands on the same `(nodeId, configHash, inputHash)`. The manual test plan already concedes there is no UI to force a miss (9.6, 'DELETE FROM activity_output_cache …').

title: Run statuses and preview rows are never pruned for deleted nodes, and `activeRunId` is not cleared on graph mutation, so a re-created node inherits the dead node's badge and preview
rationale: D11/D81/D106. `nodeStatuses` is the raw server response keyed by node id and is read as `ctx.nodeStatuses[nodeId] ?? PENDING_STATUS`; nothing removes entries for deleted nodes and the only `setActiveRunId(null)` is the replay-exit path, so editing the graph does not end the run overlay. The preview batch endpoint likewise returns every fresh row without filtering against the current config. Neither is visible while the id is gone — but with id reuse (D-021) a brand-new node renders the deleted node's success badge and its cached preview *before it has ever run*, which is precisely the corroboration a user would use to believe the wrong cache hit in D-003.
